profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility in DuPage County, Illinois, near Lemont, southwest of Chicago, is attributed to UChicago Argonne, LLC, the management and operating contractor for Argonne National Laboratory, a United States Department of Energy national laboratory. UChicago Argonne LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the University of Chicago, which has held the laboratory operating contract since Argonne founding in the 1940s as one of the first national laboratories established under the Atomic Energy Commission predecessor programs. Argonne operates significant computing infrastructure supporting its Department of Energy mission, including the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility, a Department of Energy Office of Science user facility hosting a series of major supercomputers for open scientific research. This registry facility is consistent with Argonne on site computing infrastructure supporting these programs, though a specific building name or capacity figure matching this exact facility tag was not confirmed against Argonne own published facility descriptions. As a Department of Energy contractor operated national laboratory, this facility serves federally funded scientific research rather than commercial purposes, and no commercial capacity or pricing information exists for it. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
This facility, operated by UChicago Argonne LLC for Argonne National Laboratory near Lemont, is a Department of Energy national laboratory computing installation supporting federally funded scientific research rather than commercial AI development. The facility's power capacity is not published, placing it outside the six Illinois data centers with disclosed megawatt figures, though its rank of seventh in the state reflects that other facilities of similar or smaller scale also operate without public specifications. Argonne operates the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility, a DOE Office of Science user facility hosting major supercomputers for open scientific research, and this registry location is consistent with on-site computing infrastructure supporting those programs.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities but only six with published capacity totals of 236 MW combined. This facility's unpublished capacity means the actual power available for AI computing in the state is unknown, and whether this location matters to commercial AI scaling depends entirely on whether Argonne's supercomputing mission includes work relevant to AI model development or if its infrastructure could reallocate to such work. No information is published about the facility's current utilization, tenant arrangements, or whether any compute capacity is available for purposes outside Argonne's federal research mission.
